blocks.text: Data visualization plays an important role in hypothesis testing by presenting data in a clear and understandable form. It helps researchers observe patterns, trends, and relationships in data before applying statistical tests. Visual representations make complex data easier to interpret and reduce the chances of misunderstanding results. Through charts and graphs, differences between groups can be easily compared (as shown in Figure 7.2). Visualization also assists in identifying outliers and anomalies in datasets. It supports better decision-making by providing visual evidence. Overall, data visualization strengthens the process of hypothesis testing by improving clarity and accuracy.

Scatter plot: points rising from lower left to upper right against variable 1, with one red point far from the others labelled outlier.

blocks.long_description: Each chart answers a different question: how groups compare, how things change, or how two variables move together.

blocks.text: Data visualization is important because it converts raw data into meaningful visual forms. It helps researchers quickly understand large datasets that are difficult to analyze numerically. Visual tools highlight trends, distributions, and variations in data clearly. They make communication of results easier to both technical and non-technical audiences. Visualization also reduces errors by making unusual patterns visible. It supports better interpretation of statistical findings. Therefore, data visualization is an essential step in data analysis and hypothesis testing.
Graphs and Charts for Presenting Results

Graphs and charts are commonly used tools for presenting results in hypothesis testing. Bar charts are useful for comparing categories or groups. Line graphs show trends and changes over time. Pie charts represent proportions and percentages effectively. Scatter plots display relationships between two variables. These visual tools make results more attractive, clear, and easier to interpret (as shown in Figure 7.2).

Data visuals help in directly linking results with the proposed hypothesis. They allow researchers to visually check whether the data support or reject the hypothesis. For example, a comparison graph can show differences between control and experimental treatment groups. Trends in line graphs can confirm predicted outcomes. Scatter plots help identify relationships stated in the hypothesis. Visual evidence strengthens logical reasoning in hypothesis testing. Thus, data visualization provides strong support in validating or disproving hypotheses.
